key_insight: Adaptive LLM routing can match or outperform any single model in automated heuristic discovery; larger, costlier models do not consistently produce better heuristics.
engineering_relevance: Routing heuristic-generation calls across models can improve search outcomes while reducing API costs compared with always using the strongest model.
method: Use an online bandit policy that favors rare, high-scoring heuristics over stable average performance.
Propagate credit through the heuristic population’s genealogy using a directed acyclic graph.
Discount stale observations to track each model’s changing utility during search.
evidence_signal: Across five NP-hard optimization problems and four LLMs, Ballad matched the best individual model in hindsight, sometimes surpassed every individual model, and reduced API cost by up to 65.6% relative to always using the strongest model.
watch_item: Results cover only five problems and four models; gains may depend on the model pool, task, and API pricing.
paper_title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
